learn.hook: How can a small child lift a big friend on a seesaw? The secret is a simple machine!
points: A simple machine is a tool that makes work easier. It helps us lift, move or cut things with less effort.
A lever is a strong bar that turns on a fixed point called the fulcrum. A seesaw, a hand pump handle and a bottle opener are levers.
A pair of scissors is made of two levers joined at a point.
A wheel and axle is a wheel fixed to a rod. Bicycle wheels and bullock cart wheels help us move loads easily.
A pulley is a wheel with a groove for a rope. Pulling the rope down lifts a load up, like a bucket from a well or a flag up a pole.

example.q: Think it through: Why is it easier to raise the flag on Independence Day using a pulley at the top of the pole?
steps: The flag must go up a tall pole.
Climbing the pole would be hard and unsafe.
With a pulley, we pull the rope down from the ground.
The pulley turns that pull into an upward lift.
example.answer: The pulley lets us pull down from the ground to send the flag up, which is easier and safer.

learn.reallife: Look at a hand pump. Pushing the long handle down lifts water up. The handle is a lever!

games.title: Which simple machine?
items: Rope and wheel over a well

games.title: Simple machine facts
items: A seesaw is a long bar that turns on a middle point, the fulcrum.
A pulley has a wheel with a groove for a rope.
The rope sits in the groove and runs over the wheel.
A pair of scissors is made of two levers.
The two blades turn on one pin, which is the fulcrum.
The fixed point on which a lever turns is called the fulcrum.
The lever turns around the fulcrum.

quiz.q: What does a simple machine do?
quiz.explain: Simple machines help us lift, move or cut things with less effort.
quiz.mistake: Thinks machines must be big and use electricity

quiz.q: The fixed point on which a lever turns is called the…
quiz.explain: A lever turns on a point called the fulcrum, like the middle of a seesaw.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the parts of simple machines

quiz.q: Which simple machine is used to pull a bucket of water up from a well?
quiz.explain: The rope runs over a grooved wheel. Pulling down on the rope lifts the bucket up.
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise a pulley

quiz.q: A seesaw is an example of a…
quiz.explain: A seesaw is a long bar resting on a fulcrum in the middle. That makes it a lever.
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise a lever

quiz.q: Which of these uses a wheel and axle?
quiz.explain: A bicycle's wheels turn on rods called axles.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the wheel and axle with other simple machines

quiz.q: A pair of scissors is made of how many levers?
quiz.explain: Scissors have two blades, each a lever, joined at a pin which acts as the fulcrum.
quiz.mistake: Counts the scissors as one single lever

quiz.q: Why do we use a bottle opener instead of our fingers to open a bottle cap?
quiz.explain: A bottle opener is a lever. It gives a bigger push on the cap with less effort.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how a lever helps

quiz.q: When you pull the rope of a flagpole pulley downwards, the flag moves…
quiz.explain: A pulley changes the direction of the pull. Pulling down sends the flag up.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the load moves the same way as the pull

teach.ask: Gappu saw a seesaw, a bicycle and a well with a rope. What are simple machines, and how do they help?
teach.praise: Brilliant! Levers, wheels and pulleys are simple machines that make work easier. Gappu wants to ride the seesaw!
teach.nudge: Can you name a simple machine and say how it makes work easier?

learn.hook: Why do workers roll heavy drums up a plank instead of lifting them? Let us find out!
points: A ramp, or inclined plane, is a sloping surface. It makes it easier to move heavy things up or down.
A slide in the park and a sloping path into a building are ramps.
A wedge is thick at one end and thin or sharp at the other. It is used to cut or split things, like a knife or an axe.
A screw is a rod with a groove that winds around it. The lid of a jar works like a screw.
Using a ramp, we push with less effort, but we move the load over a longer distance.

example.q: Think it through: Why do many schools and hospitals have a ramp beside the stairs?
steps: Some people use wheelchairs, prams or trolleys.
Wheels cannot easily go up steps.
A ramp is a smooth slope that wheels can roll up.
So everyone can enter the building.
example.answer: A ramp lets people in wheelchairs and with trolleys move up easily, so everyone can enter.

learn.reallife: Watch a fruit seller cut a watermelon. The knife is a wedge that splits the fruit!

games.title: Match the tool to its simple machine

items.text: An axe is a ___ that splits wood.
A sloping plank used to load a truck is a ___.
The groove that winds around a ___ helps it hold things tightly.
A ramp lets us push with ___ effort.

quiz.q: What is another name for a ramp?
quiz.explain: A ramp is a sloping flat surface, also called an inclined plane.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of simple machines

quiz.q: Which simple machine is a knife?
quiz.explain: A knife is thin and sharp at its edge. It is a wedge that pushes things apart as it cuts.
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise a wedge

quiz.q: Workers roll a heavy drum up a plank into a truck. Which simple machine is the plank?
quiz.explain: The sloping plank is an inclined plane. It makes moving the drum up easier.
quiz.mistake: Does not see a sloping plank as a simple machine

quiz.q: A jar lid turns round and round to close tightly. It works like a…
quiz.explain: The lid and the jar have grooves that wind around, like a screw.
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise the screw in everyday objects

quiz.q: Why do hospitals have ramps?
options: So wheelchairs and stretchers can move in easily
quiz.explain: Wheels can roll up a ramp but not up steps, so ramps help everyone enter.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how ramps help people with wheels

quiz.q: Which part of an axe makes it a wedge?
quiz.explain: A wedge is thick at one end and thin at the other. The sharp edge splits the wood.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what shape a wedge has

quiz.q: When we use a ramp instead of lifting a box straight up, what changes?
options: We need more effort and a shorter distance
We need less effort but move it a longer distance
quiz.explain: A ramp spreads the work over a longer path, so each push is easier.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the ramp makes the box lighter

quiz.q: Which of these is an inclined plane?
quiz.explain: A slide is a smooth slope, which is an inclined plane.
quiz.mistake: Picks a lever or pulley instead of a ramp

teach.ask: Gappu saw a ramp, a knife and a jar lid. How are they simple machines?
teach.praise: Wow! A ramp is a slope, a knife is a wedge and a jar lid is a screw. Simple machines are everywhere!
teach.nudge: What shape is a ramp? And what does a wedge do?

learn.hook: Kick a ball, open a door, fly a kite: every move starts with a push or a pull!
points: A push or a pull is called a force. Forces make things move, stop or change direction.
We push a shopping trolley to move it and pull a drawer to open it.
A force can also change the shape of things, like pressing clay or squeezing a sponge.
Things move in different ways: in a straight line (a train on a straight track), round and round (a merry-go-round) and to and fro (a swing).
Rolling is easier than sliding. That is why wheels help. A ball rolls farther on a smooth floor than on rough grass.

example.q: Think it through: Sana pushes a toy car on a smooth tiled floor and then on a rough carpet with the same push. Where will it go farther?
steps: A rough surface rubs more against the wheels.
This rubbing slows the car down.
example.answer: On the smooth tiled floor, because rough surfaces slow things down more.

learn.reallife: At the park, notice the swing going to and fro, the merry-go-round going round and round and the slide sending you down in a straight line.

games.title: Push or pull?
items: Drawing water from a well with a rope
Flying a kite on a string

quiz.q: A push or a pull is called a…
quiz.explain: Any push or pull is a force.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word force

quiz.q: How does a swing move?
quiz.explain: A swing goes forward and back again and again. That is to and fro motion.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up to and fro motion with round and round motion

quiz.q: Which of these is a pull?
options: Opening a drawer by its handle
quiz.explain: To open a drawer, we pull it towards us.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up pushing and pulling

quiz.q: Rani presses a lump of clay with her thumb and it gets a dent. What did the force do?
quiz.explain: A push can change the shape of soft things like clay.
quiz.mistake: Thinks forces can only make things move

quiz.q: Why are heavy boxes easier to move on a trolley with wheels?
quiz.explain: Wheels roll instead of rubbing along the floor, so less force is needed.
quiz.mistake: Thinks wheels change the weight of the load

quiz.q: The blades of a ceiling fan move…
quiz.explain: Fan blades turn in circles around the centre. That is round and round motion.
quiz.mistake: Does not identify circular motion

quiz.q: A ball is rolled with the same push on two surfaces. On which will it go the farthest?
quiz.explain: Grass, sand and mud are rough and slow the ball down. A smooth floor slows it the least.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how rough surfaces slow things down

quiz.q: A cricketer hits a ball and it changes direction. What made it change direction?
quiz.explain: The bat pushes the ball with a force, which changes its direction.
quiz.mistake: Does not link forces with change in direction

teach.ask: Gappu saw a ball roll, a swing sway and a fan spin. What makes things move, and in what ways?
teach.praise: Super! A push or pull makes things move, and they can move straight, round and round or to and fro.
teach.nudge: What do we need to give a ball to make it move?
